subject: Appeal: retroactive AWS Marketplace meter rate change reflected on Sep invoice
messages:
From: ACME Corp Billing <billing@acmecorp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected spike on AWS Marketplace invoice — possible retro rate apply

Hi Tessa,

We're reviewing our September AWS Marketplace invoice (invoice #ACME-202609) and see a substantial one-off charge labeled 'meter: rdx-inference-v2 - retroactive adjustment' for usage in August. This looks like a retroactive meter rate change applied after the fact.

Attached is our export of usage for Sep (acme_sept_usage_snapshot.csv) — the line items that jump are the same resource IDs we've been billed for historically. Can you confirm whether Redwood submitted any rate change request to AWS for our account or if this is an AWS-initiated pricing correction?

This is material for our finance team: if the change is retroactive we need the notice, effective dates, and guidance on refund/credit flow because VAT and withholding will be affected. High-level ask: please coordinate with AWS marketplace to get the evidence chain and let us know the remediation/credit path.

Thanks,
Lara Jenkins
Billing Manager, ACME Corp
Attachments: acme_sept_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 220 KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Corp <billing@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected spike on AWS Marketplace invoice — possible retro rate apply

Folks — looping you in. ACME found a retroactive adjustment that drove a one-time spike on their Sep invoice. They asked if this came from Redwood or AWS and need the formal evidence for VAT/refund workflows.

Quick context: we pushed the v2 inference SKU migration last quarter but no price increase was requested by Redwood to marketplace that I'm aware of. This looks like AWS applied a meter-rate correction for a rate code change (they occasionally reconcile billing on their side).

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you confirm from the marketplace onboarding logs whether Redwood submitted any price/rate-change for the affected SKU (rdx-inference-v2) between 2026-07 and 2026-09?
- Marissa: if this is AWS-initiated, we need to prepare a customer-facing note that explains the expected credit flow and the VAT handling (ACME is EU/EY legal entity). Also prepare a short mutual action plan we can send to ACME for their finance team.

I'll open a support case with AWS Marketplace and request the formal notice, meter change effective date, and appeal path. Attaching ACME's usage snapshot.

Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Finance Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_sept_usage_snapshot.csv (forwarded)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ACME Corp <billing@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Case opened: retroactive meter rate change on rdx-inference-v2 affecting ACME Corp invoice (request for evidence + appeal)

Hello AWS Marketplace Support team,

Redwood manages the rdx-inference-v2 listing (Seller ID: REDW-3377). ACME Corp (buyer account: acme-999) contacted us about an unexpected retroactive adjustment applied to their Sep invoice that references a meter/rate correction for our SKU.

Please provide the following evidence and next steps so we can coordinate with the buyer and our finance/legal teams:
1) The official notice or bulletin that announced the rate change, including the publication date and effective date.
2) The exact meter/rate code and the change history (previous rate, new rate, timestamps) tied to the resource IDs included in ACME's attached CSV.
3) A description of why the adjustment was applied retroactively rather than prospectively (if available).
4) Guidance on whether AWS issues credit memos and how VAT/withholding are handled on retroactive corrections for Marketplace invoices (we need the tax flow for ACME's EU entity).
5) Appeal instructions if the adjustment can be reversed or re-pro-rated.

We are attaching ACME's usage snapshot and our internal listing id for reference. If there's a recommended appeals form or a specific SLA for evidence requests, please escalate — ACME's month-end close timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_sept_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV), redwood_listing_map.xlsx (internal)
From: AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Corp <billing@acmecorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Case opened: retroactive meter rate change on rdx-inference-v2 affecting ACME Corp invoice (request for evidence + appeal)

Hi Tessa and team,

Thanks for the details — case CASE-98412 has been created. Summary of findings:
- Meter code: MP_RDV2_001.
- Change published: 2026-08-31 (internal bulletin ref: MKT-20260831-PRICING). Effective date listed in the bulletin: 2026-08-01.
- Change rationale: consolidation of two legacy meter tiers after detection of duplicate rate attachment to the same meter id during ingestion.
- Retroactive application: the internal reconciliation job detected overlapping rate attachments and applied corrections for the affected reporting period (July 31 -> Aug 31) which resulted in an adjustment recorded on Sep invoice.

Documents and links attached/provided:
- aws_rate_change_notice_20260831.pdf (official notice)
- internal_recon_log_excerpt.txt (redacted timestamps for the correction job)
- Credit memo process: AWS can issue a credit memo to the buyer; credits are applied to the next billing cycle unless a special settlement is requested by the seller.

Tax treatment guidance:
- AWS will issue a credit memo that references the original invoice line; VAT treatment on the credit is applied based on the buyer's country of registration and original invoice tax treatment. If ACME requires a direct refund or a reissued invoice for VAT reporting, we recommend opening a seller-assisted settlement request (SASR) and providing ACME's VAT ID so the accounting team can reissue the documents.

Appeal/reversal options:
- Appeals must be submitted within 30 days of the invoice date via the Seller Central appeals form (https://sellercentral.amazon.com/appeals) and include usage evidence and a request for withholding of credit application. We can also process a one-off special settlement if Redwood (seller) requests it and provides rationale and buyer consent.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will upload the official notice and the recon excerpt to CASE-98412 by EOD.
2) Tessa/Redwood: if you want AWS to hold credits or process a direct seller-assisted settlement (to expedite a corrected invoice for ACME), file the SASR and copy this case.
3) ACME: please share VAT ID and confirm whether you prefer a credit memo (applied to future invoices) or a reissued invoice for VAT reporting.

Let us know if you want us to escalate to billing operations for a prioritized settlement.

Best,
Priya Shah
AWS Marketplace Billing Operations
Attachments: aws_rate_change_notice_20260831.pdf (PDF, 120 KB); internal_recon_log_excerpt.txt (TXT, 8 KB)
